advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace docstring-wording greps with behavioral assertions (e.g. instantiate OutboundDiffConfig / drive compute_outbound_mutations) or scope these strictly as prose-lint, not behavior tests.
evidence: assert "used by the live reconciler" in mapping_flat
assert "create / update / delete / probe / conflict outbound leaf handlers" in outbound

These assertions grep the SOURCE UNDER TEST for docstring wording; renaming/rewording a docstring with no behavior change would fail them (refactoring-violation criterion), and no code path is exercised, so an actual behavior divergence is undetectable (regression-blindness criterion).
advisory.finding: test_rollout_headers_describe_the_live_reconciler_surfaces and test_outbound_diff_config_docs_cover_all_external_inputs_and_override_precedence assert on the docstring/prose TEXT of the source files under test (mapping_config.py, apply_outbound.py, outbound_differ.py) rather than on any observable code behavior; they are source-grepping change-detectors that break on a behavior-preserving reword and cannot detect a regression in the actual code contract they purport to protect.
scenarios: A maintainer rephrases the module header docstring without changing behavior — the test fails spuriously.
The create leaf's behavior regresses but the docstring still says the right words — the test stays green.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert against the real OutboundDiffConfig (e.g. dataclasses.fields()) and drive compute_outbound_mutations to verify mapping=/repo_root= override precedence rather than grepping the docstring.
evidence: assert f"{field}:" in text, f"{field} is undocumented in OutboundDiffConfig"
assert "Direct `mapping=` / `repo_root=` keyword arguments override" in flat
create_route.py:89-93 shows the real precedence/toggle behavior exists and is testable, but the test only greps the docstring prose in outbound_differ.py.
advisory.finding: The OutboundDiffConfig 'external inputs' test asserts each field name appears as docstring text (f"{field}:"), not that OutboundDiffConfig actually declares those fields; the config contract it claims to protect (nine caller-set fields, mapping=/repo_root= override precedence) is never exercised, so a field removed from the dataclass while left in the docstring — or a broken override precedence — passes.
scenarios: OutboundDiffConfig loses a field but the docstring still lists it — test passes (regression-blindness).
The mapping=/repo_root= override precedence inverts in code — test still green because only prose is checked.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the create_route() token sets/default/ValueError and the write-facade toggle behavior directly, deriving the doc-token check from those code constants rather than free-standing prose greps.
evidence: assert "never deletes a created issue on a post-create failure" in guide_flat
assert "legacy create+delete rollback path" in guide_flat
for token in ("legacy", "coordinator", "`0` / `false` / `off` / `no`", "`1` / `true` / `on` / `yes`"): assert token in guide_flat

create_route.py:73-74 defines _LEGACY_TOKENS/_COORDINATOR_TOKENS and :93 raises ValueError on an unknown value — none of this is exercised; only doc prose is grepped, so a token dropped from the code set while kept in the doc passes.
advisory.finding: test_operator_docs_name_rollback_values_defaults_and_consumer_specific_effects greps jira-sync-setup.md prose for behavioral claims (rollback token values, defaults, 'never deletes a created issue on a post-create failure') while the corresponding real behavior in create_route()/write-facade toggle is never exercised; the doc wording and the code can diverge with the test staying green, and any reword of the guide breaks the test.
scenarios: create_route() stops accepting 'no' as a legacy token but the guide still lists it — test passes.
The operator guide sentence is reworded harmlessly — test fails.
